findings.issue: The drag handle is a fake affordance. A 1.5x10 pill (`mx-auto mt-3 h-1.5 w-10 rounded-full bg-border`) is rendered `aria-hidden` with no pointer/touch handler, so it visually promises swipe-down-to-dismiss but does nothing. The underlying Radix Dialog (`Sheet`) has no drag-to-dismiss, so swiping the handle OR the body of the sheet is a dead gesture on every bottom sheet in the app.
findings.fix: (A) Implement drag-to-dismiss: track pointer/touch delta on the handle + sheet body, translate the SheetContent down, and call onOpenChange(false) past a ~120px/velocity threshold, snapping back below it; fire haptic("tap") on dismiss and gate the snap-back animation behind useReducedMotion(). Scope the gesture to coarse pointers (pointer-coarse) so desktop is unaffected. Alternatively remove the handle if drag isn't shipped. This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk swipe in the app — dismissing a sheet is T55's canonical case and the affordance already exists.

findings.issue: The flow renders only a Next/Finish button (right-aligned) and has NO Back/Previous control, so a student cannot revisit a prior step after advancing. T56 requires any swipe-step gesture to live 'alongside explicit Next/Back' — the explicit Back companion is absent before any swipe can be layered on, and the step index is the one place swipe-back would genuinely help.
findings.fix: (A) Add an explicit secondary Back button (left side, calls onCurrentChange(current - 1), hidden/disabled at step 0) next to the Next/Finish action; then optionally add a horizontal swipe-back between steps. Code-changeable now; the Back button is the required explicit control regardless of whether swipe is added.

findings.issue: Pinch-zoom scales the but there is no pan: the container is `overflow-hidden` and only `scale` is tracked, so at zoom>1 the off-screen edges are unreachable (zoom in on a detail you can't scroll to see). Separately, the img has `transition-transform`, so every raw onTouchMove setZoom is CSS-smoothed/lagged during an active pinch (rubbery feel), and there is no swipe-down-to-close.
findings.fix: (A) Add pan (translateX/translateY state alongside scale, reset on zoom back to 1) and drop/conditionally remove `transition-transform` while a pinch is active; (B) verify pinch+pan and an optional swipe-down-to-dismiss feel on a real device. Pan fix is codeable now; feel is device-only.

findings.issue: Multi-page PDFs render exactly one page (single canvas + `pageNum` state) and turn pages only via the ChevronLeft/ChevronRight toolbar buttons — no swipe-to-turn-page. The docstring also claims 'continuous scroll', which is not implemented (a stale/misleading comment). Explicit prev/next controls exist, so swipe is purely additive (satisfies T56), but it is missing where sequential content navigation would genuinely benefit.
findings.fix: (A) Add swipe-left/right-to-turn-page on the canvas container (touch delta threshold + haptic, disabled while zoomed so vertical scroll still works); (B) verify the scroll-vs-swipe conflict on device — when zoomed the vertical scroll must win, and only at zoom=1 should a horizontal swipe turn the page. Correct the docstring to drop 'continuous scroll'.

liveDeviceOnly: PDF swipe-to-turn-page: scroll-vs-swipe conflict (vertical scroll must win when zoomed; horizontal swipe only at zoom=1) needs a real device.
ImageViewer pinch-zoom: pan reachability and pinch feel (drop transition during active pinch) need touch hardware to verify.
MobileBottomSheet drag-to-dismiss: threshold/velocity feel and reduced-motion snap-back need a device; code is changeable now but feel is device-only.
VideoPlayer double-tap-to-seek (video-player.tsx:569-591): already additive and has an explicit scrubber, so no change required — note only.

findings.issue:
Step-to-step transition is a hard content swap: `
{renderStep(step, current)}
` re-renders with no entrance/exit, so advancing a step snaps the whole question surface. The shell has zero consumers today (grep finds only its own file), so the gap is about to propagate.

findings.issue: Progress fill animates `width` with `transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out` — a layout property (against the transform/opacity-only rule) at a non-token duration (300ms) and non-token easing (ease-out). findings.fix: (A) Replace the width transition with `animateFill(progressPercent)` (scaleX, transform) or at minimum use the token `duration-slow`/`duration-base` + `ease-snappy` instead of `duration-300 ease-out`.

findings.issue: The correct/wrong reveal (border→foreground, bg wash, dimming of unpicked rows, and the CheckCircle2/CircleX icons) snaps in with no color/border/opacity transition — the row only carries `transition-transform` for the press. findings.fix: (A) Add `transition-colors duration-fast ease-snappy` (or transition-[border-color,background-color,opacity]) to the row so the reveal is legible, and optionally `animate-enter`/popIn the check/x. findings.issue: The composer textarea uses `text-[15px]` — 15px is below iOS Safari's 16px auto-zoom threshold, so tapping it triggers a page zoom that reflows the whole transcript and can push the docked composer off-screen. This is the flagship input-heavy surface and is docked `h-dvh`, so the zoom also misaligns the keyboard-anchored layout.
findings.fix: Bump the textarea to `text-base` (16px) — the 1px difference is invisible but stops the auto-zoom. (A) code-changeable now.

findings.issue: Every input/select/textarea here uses `text-small` (0.875rem = 14px): activity, hours, date, competency select, supervisor, and the transfer-note textarea. On iOS Safari any focused control with a computed font-size <16px auto-zooms the page, so logging a contact hour on a phone zooms in on every field.
findings.fix: Switch these controls to `text-base` (16px) on mobile (keep `md:text-sm` for desktop if desired). Also note they are raw `py-2` inputs rather than `MobileInput`/`MobileTextarea` (44px min-height), so the tap target is also undersized. (A) code-changeable now.

findings.issue: Both the 'Or type your response' input and the 'Draft case title' input use `text-small` (14px) raw `py-2` inputs — iOS auto-zoom on focus, and the primary chat-type field is not the 44px touch target the flow deserves.
findings.fix: Switch to `text-base` + `min-h-11` (or `MobileInput`). (A) code-changeable now.

findings.issue: The corpus search input uses `text-sm` (14px) and `px-2 py-1` — iOS auto-zoom on focus plus a very small (~28px) tap target on a search field students are meant to use on mobile.

findings.issue: The page is `min-h-screen` (100vh = large viewport on iOS) with a vertically `flex-1 items-center justify-center` card. `interactive-widget=resizes-content` is Android-only; on iOS Safari 100vh does NOT shrink when the keyboard opens, so the Turnstile widget + 'Sign in' submit sit below the fold behind the keyboard with a centered layout that provides no scroll clearance.
findings.fix: Change the wrapper to `min-h-svh` (small viewport height, which excludes the iOS keyboard) so the form re-centers/reflows above the keyboard; verify the submit is reachable. (A) code-changeable; final behavior needs an iOS device to confirm (B).

findings.surface: MobileStickyAction over the bottom tab bar (lesson / psychopharm drug pages)
findings.issue: `--nav-h` is defined as `3.5rem` (56px) but the bottom tab bar is `min-h-14` (56px) PLUS `paddingBottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. So on a notched device (~34px inset) the sticky action's `marginBottom: var(--nav-h)` lands it 34px too low — overlapping the tab bar's icon/label row and hiding the primary submit action behind the bar.
findings.fix: Redefine the token to `--nav-h: calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` so the sticky action clears the full tab bar. (A) code-changeable now.

workstream: safearea-media (T66 mobile safe-area sweep, T69 media experience)
items: T66 Mobile safe-area sweep — every fixed/sticky/bottom/full-screen element (bottom nav, chat composer, sheets, voice UI, modals, sticky actions) must handle env(safe-area-inset-bottom)
T69 Media experience — video, audio, images, PDFs, transcripts; mobile-specific controls where desktop media interfaces add density

findings.surface: MobileStickyAction pinned above the bottom tab bar (lesson page + psychopharm drug page)
findings.issue: `offsetForNav` offsets by `marginBottom: var(--nav-h)` = 3.5rem only. The bottom tab bar is `min-h-14` (3.5rem) PLUS `paddingBottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, so the sticky bar's bottom edge lands safe-area-inset pixels INTO the tab bar (the two bars overlap by ~34px on a notched iPhone). The sticky bar ALSO applies its own `paddingBottom: max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 0.75rem)`, double-counting the inset. globals.css:206-208 comment even says 'The bar is min-h-14 + safe-area' but the token only encodes min-h-14.
findings.fix: When `offsetForNav` is true, offset by `calc(var(--nav-h) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` and drop the safe-area term from the internal paddingBottom (the tab bar already owns the inset below it). Keep `paddingBottom: max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 0.75rem)` only for the non-nav (immersive) case.

findings.surface: Notifications and Settings pages (shell routes where the top bar is present)
findings.issue: Both render `<MobilePage>` (default `inset=true`, adds `paddingTop: env(safe-area-inset-top)` + `paddingBottom`) AND `<MobileHeader>` (default `inset=true`, adds its own `paddingTop: env(safe-area-inset-top)`). The shell top bar already clears the notch (app-shell.tsx:74). Result: safe-area-top is applied THREE times (~47px x3 gap above the title on iPhone). psychopharm drug page already does this correctly with `inset={false}` + a comment; these two routes were not swept.
findings.fix: Pass `inset={false}` to both `MobilePage` and `MobileHeader` on these shell routes (or make MobilePage/MobileHeader default to `inset={false}` and opt-in on true inner pages). Mirror the psychopharm drug page.

findings.issue: `/courses/:id/materials/:id` is an inner student path, so the shell top bar is hidden (MobileBarVisibility returns null) and NOTHING provides safe-area-top. The viewer's own header (back button + title + prev/next) has no `paddingTop: env(safe-area-inset-top)`, so it renders under the notch/status bar. The container also uses `min-h-[calc(100vh-3.5rem)]` which subtracts the tab bar's min-h but not its safe-area (and uses 100vh, not dvh).
findings.fix: Add `style={{ paddingTop: 'env(safe-area-inset-top)' }}` to the header (line 71), matching simulation-header.tsx:43, and change the height to `min-h-[calc(100dvh-var(--nav-h)-env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`.

findings.surface: Lesson page drill-down (back control + title at top of viewport)
findings.issue: `/courses/:id/lessons/:id` is also an inner student path (top bar hidden), but the page's first element — the back-control row (line 178) — is plain in-flow content with no safe-area-top; ShellContent's `py-6` (24px) does not clear a ~47px notch. The back affordance and lesson title sit under the status bar on iOS.
findings.fix: Add a top inset: wrap the back-control row (or the whole page) with `paddingTop: env(safe-area-inset-top)` (e.g. `pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]` on the page root or use `MobileHeader`).

findings.issue: The scrollable body uses fixed `pb-4` (1rem) and the sheet itself (`side="bottom"`) has no safe-area-bottom. Sheets WITHOUT a footer — the session 'More' menu (session-view.tsx:356-387), HintSheet (hint-sheet.tsx:22), and the admin material action sheet in 'menu' mode (material-uploader.tsx:606-639) — let the last list item sit ~1rem from the screen bottom, under the home indicator on notched devices. Only the `footer` branch adds safe-area.
findings.fix: Make the body padding safe-area-aware when there is no footer: `pb-[max(1rem,env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]` (conditionally, so a footer doesn't double-apply), or move the safe-area onto the SheetContent container itself.

findings.surface: Custom video-player control bar in fullscreen / pseudo-fullscreen
findings.issue: `.plms-player-controls` is `bottom: 0` with `padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem 0.6rem` — no safe-area. In pseudo-fullscreen on iPhone (`.plms-player.is-pseudo-fullscreen` = `position: fixed; inset: 0`, globals.css:416-423) and native fullscreen on Android, the play/scrub/volume/fullscreen buttons sit under the home indicator / system bar. This is both a T66 (safe-area) and T69 (media control reachability) defect.
findings.fix: Change the padding to `padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem max(0.6rem, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` so the custom controls clear the inset in fullscreen/pseudo-fullscreen.

findings.issue: Pinch zoom computes `setZoom(Math.min(4, Math.max(1, (dist / basePinch.current) * 2)))` (viewer.tsx:512) — it ignores the current `zoom` state, so a second pinch after zooming resets/jumps instead of scaling from the current level. There is no `touch-action` / overscroll handling, so a pinch can also scroll the page. This is the 'image zoom' surface T69 calls out.
findings.fix: Track the zoom at pinch-start and multiply: `setZoom(clamp(startZoom * dist / basePinch) )`, and set `touch-action: none` (or `touch-action: pinch-zoom`) on the image container to stop scroll interference.

findings.surface: Audio + video mobile seek/volume sliders are hard to grab on touch
findings.issue: The audio seek (`<input type="range">`, `h-1.5 flex-1`) and the video volume slider in the mobile 'More' menu are 6px-tall native ranges with no enlarged hit area — below the ~24px minimum touch target, so scrubbing a lecture's audio or adjusting volume on a 320px screen is finicky. The PDF zoom / page nav buttons are size-10 (40px, good), but the sliders are not.
findings.fix: Increase the effective touch target: give the range inputs a taller hit region (e.g. `p-2` / `h-8` with an inner track, or wrap in a taller flex row) while keeping the visual track thin.

liveDeviceOnly: Video-player pseudo-fullscreen safe-area: needs iPhone Safari + a seeded video lesson to confirm the home-indicator overlap and that the safe-area padding fix renders correctly in pseudo-fullscreen (env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is 0 in most desktop emulators).

Image viewer pinch-zoom + touch-action behavior: needs a real touchscreen (or Playwright touch emulation with a seeded image material) to confirm pinch does not scroll the page and that the second-pinch zoom jump reproduces.

MobileStickyAction vs bottom tab bar overlap magnitude: the code under-offset is evident statically, but the exact pixel overlap on a notched device should be confirmed on hardware / a device that reports a non-zero safe-area-inset-bottom.

Lesson page + material viewer safe-area-top: confirms the ~47px notch overlap; Playwright device emulation may report safe-area-inset-top as 0, so this needs a real device or a manually-injected env() value.

findings.issue: No onboarding exists anywhere. grep for 'onboard' returns zero hits. The only first-run surface is the dashboard's 'Step 1 · Start your first course' card. An invite-only student lands straight on a course list with no orientation to the product loop (Consulting Room / daily practice / debrief). It would live as a post-login first-run flow: either a flag-guarded interstitial route (e.g. /welcome) redirected from login, or a first-run sheet gated on a profile/DB flag inside the dashboard.
findings.fix: Add a focused-steps first-run flow (one cognitive task per step: 'what is this' → 'your first practice' → 'your first case'), gated on a per-user first-login flag. Redirect target lives at login/page.tsx:18-20 (session ok → /dashboard); the first-run branch belongs there or as a dashboard-gated MobileBottomSheet.

findings.issue: Notification, camera, and storage browser permissions do not exist in the app, so T73's 'explain all four in context' overstates the real surface. No Notification.requestPermission anywhere (grep empty); notifications/page.tsx is a derived feed (T42), not push. No camera getUserMedia({video}) anywhere. No client storage-permission prompt. The ONLY real permission is the microphone (Web Speech + MediaRecorder getUserMedia({audio})).
findings.fix: Reduce T73 to mic-only. Do not build notification/camera/storage permission UI that has no runtime surface. If push/camera are ever added, add in-context copy + denial fallback then.

findings.issue: Three voice surfaces ship three divergent permission-denial treatments. voice-input.tsx is correct (context + Safari 'Access Speech Recognition' warning + 'type instead' + denial copy). voice-ask-button.tsx (Psychology Tutor) has a weaker denial string and NO Safari warning; its startMic() catch silently falls back to startWebSpeech() without surfacing the denial. dictate-conversation.tsx has the weakest: catch sets 'Microphone access denied or unavailable.' with no 'type instead' hint and no Safari warning, even though a text input sits directly below.
findings.fix: Extract one shared permission-explanation + denial-fallback component (Safari pre-warning, denied state, 'type instead' affordance) and consume it from all three surfaces.

findings.issue: session-view passes voiceAvailable as a bare prop (true), so the ChatComposer voice toggle is never disabled on browsers without STT (Firefox). A user toggles into voice mode, then VoiceInput reveals 'Voice not supported in this browser' after the fact. useVoiceSession already exposes sttAvailable/ttsAvailable.
findings.fix: Derive the toggle's availability from useVoiceSession().sttAvailable (or compute sttStatus().supported) instead of the hardcoded true.

findings.issue: voice-ask-button.tsx reimplements the entire Web Speech + MediaRecorder stack: webSpeechSupported() (44-46), inline SpeechRecognitionLike type (36-40), startWebSpeech() (49-106), and startMic() MediaRecorder→server STT (109-154). All of this already exists in src/lib/voice/stt.ts (createWebStt, sttStatus, serverTranscribe) and use-voice.ts. This is the largest single consolidation target.
findings.fix: Rewrite VoiceAskButton on useVoiceSession/createWebStt + serverTranscribe; delete the local webSpeechSupported/startWebSpeech/startMic and inline type. Keeps the continuous-recognition behavior via the shared engine or a thin wrapper.

findings.issue: dictate-conversation.tsx hand-rolls MediaRecorder recording (getUserMedia, MediaRecorder, onstop→serverTranscribe) a third time, duplicating voice-ask-button's startMic and diverging on the denial fallback.
findings.fix: Route dictation through the shared recording helper used by the other voice surfaces (or useVoiceSession), and reuse the shared permission fallback copy.

findings.issue: quiz-check.tsx still hand-rolls the exact correct/wrong reveal that MobileChoiceList was extracted to own: CheckCircle2/CircleX, border-foreground bg-primary/15, border-border bg-muted, border-border/50 opacity-60. The MobileChoiceList docstring claims QuizCheck was migrated, but it wasn't. It's a single-correct radio flow, which MobileChoiceList supports via single mode.
findings.fix: Replace the inline option-row block with MobileChoiceList (single, correct=[q.correct], picked=[picked ?? ...]); keep QuizCheck's authored-index shuffle mapping outside the list.

findings.issue: WeakSpotsDrill and ConfusableDrill hand-roll reveal states using raw Tailwind green/red (bg-green-50, border-green-500 bg-green-100, border-red-400 bg-red-100, bg-green-100 text-green-800, bg-red-100 text-red-700) — colors absent from the Neo-Brutalist Pastel token scale and not token-verified. The design system provides --status-success-bg/fg and --status-alert-bg/fg for exactly this.
findings.fix: Migrate both to MobileChoiceList reveal (check/x + tokenized fill) or, where the two-row 'weak vs strong' semantics differ, at minimum swap raw green/red for status-success/status-alert tokens.

findings.issue: viewer.tsx POSTs to /api/media/materials (body {materialId}) expecting a signed {url}, but that POST route does not exist — the only materials route is GET/HEAD /api/media/materials/[materialId] (proxy-stream, no signed URL). Every document/audio/image material therefore 404s and shows 'Couldn't open this material'. The route was refactored to proxy-stream (commit ce9690f) but the viewer was never updated — a live regression in the T70 preview path.
findings.fix: Drop the signed-URL fetch entirely: set signedUrl = `/api/media/materials/${materialId}` and pass it directly to PdfViewer/AudioViewer/ImageViewer (the GET route already streams with Range/206 + session cookie auth). Remove the POST fetch, the correlation-id fail path tied to it, and the loading skeleton's dependency on that fetch.

findings.surface: Admin submissions list (mobile: heavy list + redundant fetch)
findings.issue: SubmissionsPage does 6 parallel unfiltered `.select()` calls (submissions, assignments, lessons, courses, all student profiles, ALL submission_files) then filters/enriches entirely client-side in JS. No pagination, no server-side filter, no `.limit()`. As the cohort grows this is a heavy list + excessive network on mobile, and most fetched rows are discarded by the in-memory filter.
findings.fix: Push course/assignment/status filters into the Supabase query (`.eq()/.in()` on status + course via a join or subquery) and add `.limit()` + pagination (or at minimum a cursor). Fetch `submission_files` only for the visible page's submission ids, and `profiles` only for the emails actually needed.

findings.issue: The `useEffect` keyed on `[q, searchRetry]` fires `fetch(/api/psychopharm/search?q=...)` on every keystroke with no debounce. Typing a name like 'risperidone' issues ~11 network round-trips to an auth-gated API, causing jank and wasted requests on mobile.
findings.fix: Add a ~200ms debounce (setTimeout, cleared on each change/cleanup) before firing the fetch, or use an AbortController + debounce. Keep the existing `cancelled` flag for out-of-order responses.

findings.surface: Material upload progress bar (mobile: state understanding)
findings.issue: The upload row renders a determinate progress bar whose width is `p.progress || (status === 'preparing' ? 8 : 25)%`, but `progress` is never updated after that — the SDK exposes no byte progress (acknowledged at line 40-42). The bar sits at 25% for the whole transfer then snaps to done, which reads as a stalled/broken upload rather than an honest 'in progress' state.
findings.fix: Render an indeterminate/indeterminate-style indicator during 'uploading' (e.g. a full-width pulsing fill or a striped animated bar) instead of a fixed 25% determinate width, and reserve the determinate bar only for the confirmed 100% 'done' state.

findings.issue: VideoUpload has no size validation (unlike materials' 100MB cap via validateMaterialFile), no cancel control, and no progress — status is only idle/uploading with a spinner, and failures surface the raw Supabase error message. A large/oversized video uploads blind with no recovery except a bare error string.
findings.fix: Add a size guard before prepare (reuse/echo the media registry max), keep the label disabled during upload but add a cancel affordance, and translate the upload error into human copy (the uploader pattern in material-uploader already shows how).

findings.issue: reorderMaterials loops `await admin.from('materials').update(...)` once per material — N sequential round-trips for a lesson with many materials, each revalidating after the loop. Slow on the admin course page when reordering a long list.
findings.fix: Batch the reorder (e.g. a single upsert/update with sort_order values, or at least `Promise.all` the updates) and revalidate once at the end.

findings.surface: Dictation + tutor chat transcript rendering (mobile: heavy list)
findings.issue: dictate-conversation.tsx maps turns with `key={i}` (index key) and no memoization; tutor-chat.tsx maps messages with `key={i}` too. Long conversations re-render the entire transcript on each keystroke/turn and index keys cause needless DOM churn as entries prepend/shift.
findings.fix: Give each turn/message a stable id key, and wrap the row renderer in `React.memo` so only the new/edited bubble re-renders. Low-cost, no virtualization needed at these sizes.

liveDeviceOnly: Verify the viewer fix against a real seeded material with a live session (GET proxy-stream Range/206 for pdf.js, audio seek, image display) — code fix is static but playback needs Supabase storage + dev server.
Confirm submissions-page pagination/filter performance at cohort scale (seeded DB with many submissions/files) — the N+1 today is only observable with real row volume.
Confirm upload progress/cancel UX against live Supabase Storage (byte progress unavailable by SDK — the indeterminate-bar change needs a real slow upload to eyeball).
